title: Fever in Adults: Purpose, Management, and Warning Signs
content:
A fever is a temporary elevation in body temperature, defined clinically as a core body temperature of 100.4°F (38.0°C) or higher. Fever is not an illness itself, but an orchestrated physiological immune defense triggered by pyrogens when the hypothalamus elevates the body's internal thermostat to combat viral or bacterial infections.

General Home Management for Adults:
- Hydration: Increase fluid consumption significantly (water, electrolyte solutions, clear broths, herbal teas). Sweating from fever rapidly depletes fluid reserves.
- Rest: Conserve metabolic energy by resting quietly in bed.
- Comfortable Ambient Temperature: Dress in lightweight, breathable cotton clothing and sleep under a light sheet. Avoid bundle-wrapping, which can trap excess heat, and never use cold ice baths or alcohol rubs, as they cause shivering and drive core temperature higher.
- Monitoring: Track temperature every 4 to 6 hours using an oral or infrared digital thermometer.

When to Seek Immediate Medical Evaluation:
- Body temperature reaches or exceeds 103°F (39.4°C) or fails to drop after antipyretic administration.
- Fever lasting continuously longer than 3 full days (72 hours).
- Severe accompanying symptoms: stiff neck and inability to bend chin to chest, confusion or extreme drowsiness, shortness of breath, unexplained widespread skin rash, or persistent vomiting with inability to retain fluids.
- In infants under 3 months: any rectal temperature of 100.4°F (38.0°C) or higher requires immediate emergency department evaluation.
source_name: Mayo Clinic & American College of Emergency Physicians
